source: LOC draft-04, MSF draft-01; derived from the Python Video.js example and Video.js media/moq. Boundary cases derived from encoding rules. Numeric inputs and LOC integer values are decimal strings; catalog json is the exact expected UTF-8 document. parsed is what both catalog readers return for a json document: camelCase fields, namespaces as tuples, init data as hex, absent optional fields omitted. Every catalogs document must read back as its parsed value with the input namespace as the catalog namespace; endCatalogs are msf-01 §11.3 end-of-broadcast documents, read back the same way; catalogReads are parse-only documents from other producers or edge cases; catalogReadErrors must be rejected by both readers. Media Timeline vectors (msf-01 §7, issue #291): timelineEntries map a broadcast-timeline timestamp, a location and an optional wall-clock time that defaults to the timestamp (decimal strings) to one record; timelines are records in, exact json out, read back as the same records; timelineReads are parse-only payloads; timelineEntryErrors, timelineErrors and timelineReadErrors must be rejected by both languages. Records are written as msf-01 writes them, [mediaTimeMs, [group, object], wallclockMs], with plain JSON numbers. locTimestamps (issue #290) read an object's LOC Timestamp in microseconds from its properties ([type, decimal value] pairs), optional track properties and an optional catalog timescale; timestampUs null means no usable Timestamp.

catalogReads.name: lenient-fields
catalogReads.source: Synthetic: msf-01 says a parser MUST ignore fields it does not understand. Wrong-typed and non-integral count fields are ignored, entries without a string name are skipped, unknown or non-inline init references resolve to nothing, and base64 is decoded as atob does.

catalogReads.source: msf-01 §5.6.9's timeline entry, with a non-string item in depends; a second entry has a wrong-typed mimetype and depends. depends keeps its string items; both fields are read only with their JSON type.
